side_effects.x87_state: the current x87 control word is replaced by (CW & 0xF3FF) | 0x0C00; the previous control word is not restored
side_effects.global_state: the 16-bit global at 0x006E5BC4 is overwritten with the current CW, then ORed with 0x0C00, then used as the source of fldcw; it remains modified after return

rounding_semantics.observed_sequence: fwait; fnstcw word [0x006E5BC4] (store current CW); or word [0x006E5BC4],0x0C00 (set bits 10 and 11); fldcw word [0x006E5BC4] (load the modified CW); ret
rounding_semantics.control_word_bits: x87 CW bits 10-11 are the rounding-control field: 00 nearest, 01 down, 10 up, 11 truncate/chop. OR with 0x0C00 sets both bits to 1 while leaving the other 14 control bits unchanged.
rounding_semantics.equivalent_expression: CW = (CW & 0xF3FF) | 0x0C00; no AND instruction is needed because OR with 1s overwrites exactly those two bits
rounding_semantics.previous_state: not saved for restoration and not restored by this function; the 16-bit slot at 0x006E5BC4 is overwritten on every call
rounding_semantics.scope: the effect is on the x87 control word of the calling thread; this analysis did not observe any thread state at runtime. The bit assignments are architectural x86 facts, not runtime observations from this game.

independent_reanalysis.detail: The retail image was re-read byte-exactly with objdump and capstone, then re-analysed with Binary Ninja MCP, radare2 6.2.0 and angr 10.0.4.post1. Binary Ninja is the only decompiler used in this corrected pass. The prior Ghidra pass is retained only as superseded historical evidence.

observed_facts.fact: The hashed image is PE32, machine i386, preferred image base 0x00400000, Windows GUI subsystem, .text at VA 0x00401000 with virtual size 0x00132000. SHA-256 is dea34892d417715873ea61d7b2ba5556655f1ad65385104348146f9679915a01 and MD5 is 9d8ebb7f28a1be56a8626dd5948826e4.
The function at 0x00498460 spans 0x00498460-0x00498476 inclusive, 23 bytes (0x17). It is not 17 bytes and does not end at 0x00498470. The byte at 0x00498477 is 0x90 padding.
observed_facts.evidence: C2, C8; BN range 0x498460-0x498477 (23 bytes); r2 size 23; angr size 0x17

observed_facts.fact: The retail instruction sequence is: fwait (9B); fnstcw word [0x006E5BC4] (D9 3D C4 5B 6E 00); or word [0x006E5BC4],0x0C00 (66 81 0D C4 5B 6E 00 00 0C); fldcw word [0x006E5BC4] (D9 2D C4 5B 6E 00); ret (C3).
Binary Ninja reports one basic block, 23 bytes, zero calls and zero edges. radare2 reports num-bbs 1, num-instrs 5 and args 0; angr reports one block and size 0x17.

The function reads no stack arguments and has no ESP- or EBP-relative memory operand; Binary Ninja's stack layout contains only __return_addr and no local variables. It uses no stack allocation and ends with a plain C3 ret. Binary Ninja's x87control parameter and int32_t return are decompiler modeling artifacts, not evidence of a real stack argument or EAX return.

The function touches the 16-bit global at 0x006E5BC4: fnstcw writes the current control word, OR 0x0C00 modifies bits 10-11 in place, fldcw reads the result. All three references to 0x006E5BC4 are inside this function. The byte-exact scan finds the four-byte value at file offsets 0x98463, 0x9846a and 0x98472 (VAs 0x498463, 0x49846A, 0x498472).

The semantic effect is CW := CW | 0x0C00, equivalently (CW & 0xF3FF) | 0x0C00: rounding control becomes 11 (truncate/chop), all other control bits are preserved, and the previous CW is not restored. The global at 0x006E5BC4 remains modified.

Exactly five direct call instructions target 0x00498460: 0x0048F7A5, 0x0048F80D, 0x0048F9EA, 0x004925FC, 0x0049427F. Binary Ninja and radare2 both list the same five; there are no E9/EB jumps and no stored dword literal equal to the VA.

0x0048F9EA is reached only when the window-procedure param equals 0x1C. The dispatch first compares EDI with 0x1C and uses ja to send greater values to 0x0048F9F8; the je then reaches 0x0048F9EA. After the call the procedure returns 0 via xor eax,eax and ret 0x10.
0x001C is the documented Win32 WM_ACTIVATEAPP value; WM_ACTIVATE is 0x0006. The compared immediate is not a retail-only constant and is not WM_ACTIVATE.
observed_facts.evidence: Win32 platform constant; C9 and C10 confirm the compared immediate is 0x1C

observed_facts.fact: 0x0048F7A5 immediately follows the setter call at 0x0048F7A0 in the window-creation routine, so the retail code stores the CreateWindowExA handle before it forces truncating rounding.
observed_facts.evidence: C8 in the 0x0048F0A0 record; C10; r2/objdump window-creation walk

observed_facts.fact: The contexts of 0x004925FC and 0x0049427F were not classified. Binary Ninja reports caller symbols Display_InitDirectDraw and Display_RestoreDevice_6, but these are database annotations and are not treated as behavior evidence.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The setter is used to force truncating rounding for subsequent x87 float work after window creation and on WM_ACTIVATEAPP.
hypotheses.basis: The call sites and the forced RC bits; the intended numerical reason is not documented in the image.
All three references are inside this function and the value is not restored by it.
hypotheses.status: supported by the reference census; still an inference about intent

hypotheses.hypothesis: The game treats message 0x1C as WM_ACTIVATEAPP.
hypotheses.basis: The value matches the Win32 constant and the response is an FPU-state reset.

unresolved.item: The contexts and purposes of call sites 0x004925FC and 0x0049427F are unknown.
Other code elsewhere in the image contains fldcw instructions (for example 0x004A9D46, 0x004A9D70, 0x004A9DD5); whether any of them restores a different rounding mode later is not analysed here.
The effect on individual floating-point operations, exception masks and precision control is not evaluated; only the control-word bits are analysed.
Why a global scratch is used rather than a stack slot is not established; the described stack-based sequence is absent from the image.
The function has no symbol name; 'x87 truncate-rounding setter' is descriptive, and Display_ClearSurfaces_16 is a Binary Ninja database annotation.
The actual x87 control-word value at any call site was not observed at runtime.

limitations: Static analysis only. No runtime, behavioural or paired retail/candidate evidence exists for this record, and none is implied.

Binary Ninja MCP was reachable for this corrected pass and is the single decompiler used here. The earlier pass used Ghidra 12.1.2 only because the BN endpoint had returned no_active_binary_view at that time; that Ghidra output is retained only as superseded history and is not used for any conclusion.

The earlier pass produced an incorrect size for this function: it claimed 17 bytes ending at 0x00498470 with a stack-local sequence and no global access. That was wrong. The corrected retail facts are 23 bytes (0x00498460-0x00498476), a global control-word slot at 0x006E5BC4, no stack local, and a plain C3 ret at 0x00498476. The correction is based on the byte-exact image, Binary Ninja, radare2 and angr.

The earlier pass also described the calling convention as void/unknown and used Ghidra's folding of the wait prefix. Binary Ninja keeps fwait as a separate instruction and reports five instructions; the byte extent and effect are unchanged.
No candidate source was reviewed or compared, and no CFG-similarity score or structural-verification claim is made.
The function name is descriptive only; the retail PE provides no source-level name for this address.

The byte census of callers covers direct E8/E9/EB encodings in the .text section and stored dword literals equal to the target VA across the whole file. It cannot rule out an indirect call whose address is computed rather than stored as a literal.
objdump emits AT&T syntax (source, destination order); the Intel-style listings in this record come from Binary Ninja and radare2.
Binary Ninja's data-xref query returned 0 rows for 0x006E5BC4. The three-reference count is established by the byte-exact scan, objdump and radare2, not by BN data xrefs.
The x87 control-word field assignments (bits 10-11, 11 = truncate) are architectural facts about the x86 FPU, not runtime observations from this game.
No later control-word state was observed, so the claim that truncating mode remains in force beyond the function is not made.
The BN Pseudo C for fnstcw/fldcw uses intrinsic pseudo-arguments; it is not literal C and is not used as a signature source.
No runtime execution, Frida/IGI-Probe capture, candidate build or paired comparison was performed.
